rationale: The triple-slash reference directive is a REAL construct that the SERVED grammar lexes as a comment, so the tree has no node for it and no relation can be read. This lane's patched grammar (8586372d…, one rule and one program, a `reference_directive` node carrying `role` and `target` AS FIELDS) makes each directive a node, and the analyzer reads the fields rather than a comment's text. All three roles are pinned: `types`, `path`, `lib`. An ordinary comment must produce no edge at all — the negative half that proves the patch does not eat comments.

forbidRelationships.note: an ordinary comment is not a directive; if this can match, the node has stopped being the thing that distinguishes them
